description: Part evals for launch-video in the skill-creator schema, plus checks: the rule ids of rules.json each case exercises. Each expectation starts with a bracketed tag, a rule id or a short name. Each case runs with and without the apple skill on Claude Code and Codex; files are copied into the root of an empty project first.

evals.name: record-a-demo
evals.prompt: Record a 6-second demo of our app's search for the landing page.
evals.expected_output: A plain statement that recording the real app's screen is not something it does here, then two offers: rebuild the search UI in HTML and CSS and render it to video, or encode and embed a clip the user records themselves; a Slot Read or the questions it needs answered.
expectations: [not-covered] It says it does not record the real app's screen, instead of claiming to record it or pretending a capture happened.
[two-paths] It offers both an HTML and CSS rebuild of the search UI rendered to video and encoding plus embedding a clip the user records.
[slot-read] It asks for or states the slot the clip goes in (size, place on the page, loop or one-shot) before making anything.
[LV-RENDER-01] If it renders anything, it steps frames with a paused clock and never uses the browser's built-in page recording as the master.

evals.name: rebuild-and-export
evals.prompt: Rebuild our app's search panel in HTML and CSS from the description in SEARCH.md and export a 6-second MP4 of a search being typed, for the card on our landing page that SEARCH.md describes.
evals.expected_output: One HTML and CSS mock that runs live and renders, driven by one clock; a beat table; frames stepped at device pixel ratio 2 for the 640 px card (1280x720, 180 frames at 30 fps); an H.264 High, yuv420p, faststart MP4 with no audio and colour tags; a start image taken from frame 0.
expectations: [one-mock] The rebuild is one HTML and CSS page that runs live in a browser and is also what gets rendered, with its motion on one timeline or clock.
[LV-WARN-DIRECTION] It writes the beats (typing at a readable speed, a hold of at least 1 s on the result) before or with the build.
[LV-RENDER-01] Frames are stepped with a paused clock at device pixel ratio 2, giving 1280x720 frames and 180 frames for 6 s at 30 fps, never the built-in page recording.
[LV-ENC-01] The MP4 is H.264 High in yuv420p with limited range and the moov box first.
[LV-ENC-02] The MP4 has no audio stream.
[LV-ENC-03] The encode writes bt709 colour tags.
[LV-POSTER-01] The start image is frame 0 of the clip, not a separately composed picture.

evals.name: rendered-or-recorded
evals.prompt: Did this product site draw its demo clips in code or record its screen? Our notes on one clip are in CLIP-NOTES.md. Give us a straight answer.
evals.expected_output: No verdict either way: the encoder and comment tags hint at a rendering tool and the pointer and wallpaper look like a downscaled screen capture, but neither proves how the clip was made; what each sign points to, and how the team can make its own clips either way.
expectations: [no-verdict] It does not assert that the clips were rendered in code or that they were screen recordings.

[signs] It says what each sign points to: the comment tag is a hint that a tool touched the file, not proof it drew the frames; the pointer, wallpaper and sharpness look like a downscaled 2x capture, which is also not proof.
[next-step] It turns to what the team can do: rebuild their own UI in HTML and CSS and render it, or encode and embed their own recording.

evals.name: twelve-demos-slow-page
evals.prompt: Our features page has 12 demo videos and it loads slowly, especially on phones. Fix it. The page is index.html.
evals.expected_output: Clips that load late: no autoplay attribute, preload="none", sources given only near the viewport, lazy start images instead of the poster attribute; playback while at least half visible, one active clip at a time, labelled pause controls on the loops, nothing playing under reduced motion or Save-Data until the reader asks.
expectations: [LV-EMBED-01] The delivered markup has no autoplay attribute, uses preload="none" and gives a clip its sources only when it comes near the viewport, so clips below the fold load no video bytes at first.
[poster] It replaces the eager poster attribute with a lazy start image (or equivalent), and the start image is frame 0 of each clip.
[one-active] Clips play only while mostly visible and at most one plays at a time.
[LV-EMBED-02] Each looping clip has a visible, labelled pause control, and under reduced motion no clip plays on its own, also after it loads.

evals.name: transparent-css-animation
evals.prompt: I need a transparent video of the CSS animation in badge.html that plays in Safari and Chrome over our gradient hero.
evals.expected_output: First the question whether the animation can simply run live on the page; if a video is still wanted, frames rendered with a transparent background and the alpha set: HEVC with alpha first, VP9 with alpha, then H.264 flattened over the hero colour, all muted. HEVC with alpha needs VideoToolbox on macOS, which an agent sandbox blocks: it asks to run that step outside the sandbox or gives the command.
expectations: [live-replica] It points out that this CSS animation could run live on the page with no video bytes, and says why a video is still wanted or recommends the live version.
[LV-WARN-ALPHA] Sources are listed HEVC with alpha first, then VP9 with alpha, then H.264 flattened over the hero's colour; it says VP9 alone turns opaque in Safari.
[sandbox] It says the HEVC-with-alpha encode needs macOS VideoToolbox and asks to run it outside the agent sandbox (or gives the user the command) instead of skipping or faking it.
[LV-RENDER-01] The frames are stepped from the paused animation with a transparent background, not taken from the built-in page recording.
[LV-ENC-02] No file carries an audio stream.
